question: Who achieved fame for the Pandanallur school of Bharatanatyam?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Meenakshi Pillai__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the most prominent and popular classical dance forms that originated in Tamilnadu, India.
 
• It is strengthened and nourished by various styles - Pandanallur, Kalakshetra, Melattur, Tanjore, Vazhuvoor etc.
 
• **Pandanallur **style gives a lot of emphasis on Abhinaya. Stomping or strong tapping on the floor is discouraged in this style. Instead, the focus is on expressive movements which makes the Salangai render melodious music and rhythm.
 
• **Pandanallur **style was mainly attributed to **Shri. Meenakshisundaram Pillai.**
 
 
• He was a dance guru who lived in the village of Pandanallur, in the Thanjavur district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
 
• He was popularly known as **thatha**.
 
• Meenakshisundaram Pillai belonged to the lineage of the Thanjavur Quartet, who were patronised by the Maratha kings of Thanjavur.
 
• His expertise was not only in dance but also in music. Besides dancing and singing, Meenakshisundaram could play the veena, mridangam, and other instruments.
 
• He had a flair for languages and was fluent in Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu and Malayalam.
 
• His students such as Rukmini Devi, Mrinalini Sarabhai, Ram Gopal, Shanta Rao, and, more carried the Pandanallur flag to the international stage.
